catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alejandro-her: This 1913 reference piece on Alexandre Herculano — the great historian of Portugal — tells his full story. Jeremiah Ford follows his life. His pen fought for a free press. Exile in England taught him much. His novels brought old Portugal alive. His history remains the classic work.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antonio-de-ar: A 1913 entry on Antonio de Araujo — a name in the mission story. The entry preserves his modest fame. The missions remember their workers. The old chronicles keep his name. A laborer of the distant missions. His mission served the frontier villages.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antonio-espej: A 1913 entry on Antonio Espejo — the explorer of New Mexico. James Mooney tells his bold entrada. He sought the fabled northern riches. His report mapped the Pueblo lands. A pioneer of the Southwest. His name marks the New Mexican maps.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-cristobal-de-: A 1913 entry on Cristóbal de Castillejo — the Spanish poet. Ventura Fuentes honors his famous verse. His pen scourged the Italianate fashion. The court prized its witty satirist. The singer of the old Castilian muse. His Diálogo is famed.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-francisco-de-: This 1913 reference piece on Francisco de Araújo — the Dominican theologian. William Noon notes his famous works. The entry preserves his modest fame. His pen served the seventeenth century. A friar among the schoolmen. His 1635 works are famed.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ghirlandajo: A 1913 entry on Ghirlandaio — the Florentine master. Louis Gillet honors his famous frescoes. His brush crowned the Medici chapels. The city prized the gifted hand. The teacher of the young Michelangelo. His 1494 death is famed.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-portoviejo: Portoviejo, the Manabí city of Ecuador's coast, became a diocese. This entry covers its bishops, churches, and history as of 1913. The faith in the land of the ceibo trees: its modest cathedral serves all of coastal Manabí province faithfully.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-st-toribio-al: St. Toribio Mogrovejo was the archbishop of Lima. This entry traces his visitations, his Indians, and his fame. The apostle of the Peruvian church: his great see crowned Lima in the 1580s' Peru in the city of the kings in America.
